claims.text: An ML surrogate trained on explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics data from both solid and fluid phases can predict the phase free-energy landscape.
A limited or sparse ab initio training set is sufficient for the proposed free-energy surrogate.
The surrogate can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can approach the energy and force accuracy of their underlying DFT calculations in multicomponent refractory alloys.
Moment tensor potentials provide a favorable balance between computational cost and accuracy.
The proposed target domain consists of multicomponent high-entropy systems in solid and fluid states near fusion.
The intended temperature range extends from approximately 0.9 times the melting temperature to fusion temperatures.
Vibrational entropy, anharmonic effects, and electron–vibration contributions are critical in the stated near-fusion temperature range.
Local atomic configurations and bonding environments encode the interactions governing phase free energies.
A surrogate trained on representative configurations can interpolate thermodynamic properties with high fidelity.
Using the surrogate reduces the number of expensive first-principles calculations or simulations required.
The cost reduction can be achieved while preserving entropy and anharmonic contributions to the free energy.
The surrogate will provide at least an order-of-magnitude speedup relative to explicit ab initio MD and TOR-TILD.
Fusion free energies and related observables will be predicted within approximately 5% of the explicit ab initio MD or TOR-TILD results.
Explicit ab initio MD free-energy calculations and TOR-TILD provide high accuracy but are prohibitively expensive for multicomponent systems.
The proposed method is expected to remain valid for systems containing up to approximately five elements.
Performance beyond the stated composition and temperature limits is unknown.
The surrogate may fail to capture extreme anharmonicity and subtle electron–vibration coupling at the highest temperatures.
Out-of-training-set phase free energies, entropy contributions, coupling indicators, and runtime can be benchmarked against explicit ab initio MD or TOR-TILD.
An error exceeding 5% or a speedup below tenfold constitutes falsification.
